solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Musician, learner with hesitation, was flat unfortunately to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with places the rearranged letters at the front, ahead of the other pieces
unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so the words 'was flat' are scrambled

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate abbreviation
er is the sound of a speaker hesitating

explanation.surface: A musician, still a beginner and hesitant, played flat from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks musical, as a note sung off pitch, but just gives letters to shuffle; 'to begin with' sets those shuffled letters ahead of the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Fats Waller was a celebrated American jazz pianist and composer, so a musician.

clue.text: Hero is a 'card' wanting a kiss

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for the jack, a playing card
X is the conventional kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A hero, a real joker of a fellow, is longing for a kiss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'card' looks like a comic person; here it is a playing card, the jack, J. 'wanting' just links, meaning needing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax was a mighty Greek warrior of the Trojan War, a classical hero.

clue.text: Seaside town struggles with summer finally gone

indicators.note: gone says a letter disappears from the word for struggles

parts.note: struggles means strives

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word summer

explanation.surface: A resort town battles on now that the summer season is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes R from summer; 'gone' removes it from STRIVES. ST IVES is a Cornish seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: St Ives is a well-known coastal resort town in Cornwall, England.

clue.text: Using some upsetting rhetoric, I am a ranter in mostly obsolete language

indicators.note: upsetting says the hidden letters are read backwards
Using some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A self-confessed ranter admits to spouting overturned rhetoric in a dead tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition began with 'in', which only links wordplay to definition; the definition is the noun phrase after it. 'upsetting' turns CIAMARA round.
explanation.definitionFit: Aramaic, the tongue of Jesus's time, survives only in small communities, so it is largely extinct.

clue.text: Abode in narrow passage, we hear

definitions.note: abode here is the past tense of abide, meaning stayed or rested, matching the past participle of lie

indicators.note: we hear says the word is identified by how it is spoken

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road or passage

explanation.surface: Someone's home is said to be tucked in a little alley.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abode' looks like a noun, a dwelling, but is the verb: abided, stayed put.
explanation.definitionFit: To abide is to remain or rest somewhere, as to lie is to stay in place; both past forms.

clue.text: Managed flattering attention — no time to show ill will

parts.note: managed, as in ran a business

indicators.note: no says a letter is left out of the word for flattering attention

parts.note: to court someone is to pay flattering attention; court as a noun

explanation.surface: Someone managed to flatter without wasting time, yet still shows resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is bitter, long-lasting resentment, a synonym for ill will.

clue.text: Perfect short story enthralling tot with mum

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so the story's letters hold the others

parts.note: a conte is a short story, especially a French tale
to tot up is to add, so a tot is a sum
ma is a familiar word for mother

explanation.surface: A perfect little tale that keeps a toddler and its mother spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' is not a toddler but an addition: tot up a SUM.
explanation.definitionFit: Consummate as an adjective means supremely accomplished, complete, flawless: synonymous with perfect.

clue.text: Flirts with wandering hands — peril!

indicators.note: wandering means straying about, so these letters stray into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone flirting with roving hands is in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A philanderer has casual affairs; to philander is to flirt or womanise, so he flirts.

clue.text: One to rescue limited number, going to a height

parts.note: No. is number cut short, its abbreviation

explanation.surface: A rescuer saves just a few people by climbing to a high place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limited number' reads as a few survivors, but it is number abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Noah built the ark and saved his family and the animals from the Flood.

clue.text: Beginners' alphabet in wording under diagram could be taxing

definitions.note: a noun for a tax, defined loosely by the phrase about what may tax people

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a caption is the text under an illustration
ITA is the Initial Teaching Alphabet, once used to teach children reading

explanation.surface: Explaining a teaching alphabet in the text beneath a diagram might prove demanding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taxing' suggests difficult, but means levying tax. ITA was a phonetic alphabet used in British schools in the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: Capitation is a levy of a fixed sum per head, a poll tax, so it is a form of taxation.

clue.text: Government agent against despot, not half

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons

indicators.note: not half says only the first portion of the ruler's title stays

parts.note: a sultan is an absolute ruler

explanation.surface: An official representative opposes a tyrant, though only half-heartedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A consul is an official appointed by a state to represent it and its citizens abroad.

clue.text: Space traveller by himself with a bit of personality

parts.note: per se is Latin for by itself or in itself
the id is a part of the psyche in Freudian theory

explanation.surface: A lone astronaut with only a touch of character.
explanation.definitionFit: The Perseids are an annual meteor shower; each meteor speeds through space.

clue.text: Estate office has scheme to replace its head

indicators.note: to replace its head says the first letter of the office word is swapped for another piece

parts.note: a station is a post or office, as in police station
a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: An estate agency's office has a plan to replace its boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A plantation is a large farming estate, where crops such as tea or cotton are grown.

clue.text: Noteworthy as script from borderline candidate might be?

definitions.text: as script from borderline candidate might be
definitions.meaning: an exam paper near the pass mark may need marking a second time

explanation.surface: A borderline candidate's exam paper is worth noting for a second look.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as RE-MARKABLE: able to be marked again.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable means worthy of remark or attention, so striking and notable.

clue.text: Dog beginning to dig place for the bone?

indicators.note: beginning to selects the opening letter of dig

parts.note: a dog buries its bone in a hole

explanation.surface: A dog starts to dig a spot to bury its bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The dhole is a wild canine of Asia, a red-coated hunting species.

clue.text: Author's car

definitions.meaning: the 's stands for is; Philip ... wrote His Dark Materials

explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', so the author is the answer as well as the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Pullman is a British novelist; a Pullman is a comfortable railway coach.

clue.text: What's formal and stuffy about a king

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for stuffy goes round the letter

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and proper

explanation.surface: Asks what's stiff and starchy about a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the king of Troy in Greek legend, father of Hector and Paris.

clue.text: Fish caught — endless hassle

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: endless says the final letter of the word for hassle drops off

parts.note: to harry is to hassle or harass

explanation.surface: An angler lands a fish after an interminable struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: Charr (also char) is a cold-water fish of the trout and salmon family.

clue.text: Ends with wounds, head being covered

indicators.note: head being covered means the opening letter is hidden from view

parts.note: maims means wounds, injures

explanation.surface: A tale ends with injuries, a head being bandaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ends' looks like conclusions; here it means goals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ends here are purposes or goals, so a synonym of aims as a plural noun.

clue.text: Aspect of moon's appearance said to unsettle

indicators.note: said signals that the spoken form is what counts

parts.note: a phase is the moon's apparent shape at a given time, such as crescent

explanation.surface: How the moon looks is supposedly enough to disturb someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To faze someone is to disconcert or disturb them, a synonym of unsettle.

clue.text: Cold fish

definitions.meaning: chilly and exposed, as of a windswept landscape
a small silvery freshwater fish of the carp family

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as 'cold fish', an unfriendly person, but splits into two separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Bleak weather is cold and raw; the bleak is also a small European river fish.

clue.text: One of the top priests, a clever person protecting the Queen

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding as a shield, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: a brain is an informal word for a clever person
HM stands for Her Majesty

explanation.surface: A senior priest, a bright individual, guards the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahmins form the highest Hindu caste, traditionally the priestly class.

clue.text: What you get in some bars — strong Asian drink served up, all right?

definitions.text: What you get in some bars

indicators.note: served up, in a down clue, means the drink's letters go upwards, so backwards

parts.note: arak (arrack) is a strong spirit distilled in Asia
oke is a dictionary variant of okay, meaning all right

explanation.surface: In certain bars a potent Eastern spirit is poured, and all is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' reverses ARAK to KARA; 'bars' suggests drink but means pubs where people sing.
explanation.definitionFit: Karaoke, singing along to recorded backing tracks, is entertainment offered in many pubs and clubs.

clue.text: Before the start of event formidable person will be dressing

indicators.note: Before places the formidable person in front of the other piece

parts.note: a tartar is a fierce, intimidating person

indicators.note: the start of selects the first letter of event

explanation.surface: Before the event begins, a fearsome figure will be getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressing' suggests putting clothes on; it is a sauce. TARTARE here is short for tartare sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Tartare sauce is a mayonnaise-based condiment served with fish, a type of dressing.

clue.text: Shopping area? Then for demolition use hammer

parts.note: a mall is a shopping centre

indicators.note: for demolition suggests knocking down and rebuilding, so the letters of use are rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopping centre is to be torn down, so use a hammer.
explanation.definitionFit: The malleus is the small bone of the middle ear, Latin for hammer and named after its shape.

clue.text: Time for eating less? I left food

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: At a time to cut down, someone walked away from the meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lentil is an edible pulse, a seed eaten in soups and stews.

clue.text: Former PM ignoring the Queen — hairy stuff?

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so the royal letters go

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher was British Prime Minister from 1979 to 1990
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister snubs the monarch, over hair perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the jokey definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatch is a humorous word for a thick head of hair, as well as roof straw.

clue.text: Cut down on fat — get some fruit

indicators.note: cut down means shortened, so the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: plump means fat, chubby

explanation.surface: Reduce your fat intake by eating some fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The plum is a stone fruit, a common example of fruit.

clue.text: Workers in county briefly taking hour off

indicators.note: taking ... off says a letter is removed from the county's short name
off completes 'taking off', removing something from the county

parts.note: Hants is the short form of Hampshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Workers in a shire take an hour's break.
explanation.walkthrough: HANTS is the standard abbreviation of Hampshire, a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Worker ants do the colony's labour, so ants are a classic example of workers.

clue.text: Two wines, litres being drunk? I'm not happy

indicators.note: being drunk means being swallowed, so the first wine takes in the litres

parts.note: Macon is a French Burgundy wine
tent is an old Spanish red wine

explanation.surface: After two bottles and litres downed, someone complains of unhappiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' suggests intoxication, but says the litres are swallowed by the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A malcontent is a dissatisfied, grumbling person, who might say these words.

clue.text: Paint stains son initially removed

indicators.note: initially removed says the letter goes from the front

parts.note: soils means stains, dirties

explanation.surface: Paint marks a son left at first, a messy child.
explanation.definitionFit: Oils are oil paints, the medium of oil painting, so a kind of paint.

clue.text: Very many like identification using letters only?

definitions.meaning: a code with no digits, only letters

explanation.surface: Countless IDs use letters only.
explanation.definitionFit: Numberless means countless, too many to number, so very many.
